natural-roll-quick.title: Natural roll
natural-roll-quick.purpose: Recognize natural rolling departures and distinguish them from stun.
natural-roll-quick.instruction: Use a moderate cut and little sidespin. Allow natural roll at contact. Compare the eventual rolling direction with the approximately 30-degree reference when shown, then restore and test stun.
natural-roll-quick.success: Explain which trial arrives rolling and which arrives in stun. Predict the departure side before three different cuts; the 30-degree reference is an approximation over its useful hit range.
natural-roll-quick.transfer: Recreate the cut and observe the cue-ball route from rolling and stun deliveries. Use the direction as a starting reference, then check it on your table.
natural-roll-quick.progression: Compare a fuller and a thinner hit to learn where the natural-angle approximation stops being useful.

physics-follow-quick.purpose: Control forward cue-ball travel after pocketing a straight shot.
physics-follow-quick.instruction: Choose a finish beyond the collision point and away from a pocket. Hold aim and speed fixed; compare two small follow settings and watch the stopping distance.

physics-draw-quick.instruction: Keep the shot straight and sidespin at zero. Choose a return zone. Compare draw at a fixed speed, reset, then compare speed at a fixed draw setting.

physics-stun-quick.title: Stop and stun

physics-stun-quick.instruction: Keep sidespin at zero. Compare the tangent reference with the initial path after collision. Adjust tip height or speed to approach stun; then compare follow and draw.
physics-stun-quick.success: Predict the initial exit side on three cuts, then record the pot and whether the initial route follows your tangent reference. Do not grade the entire follow/draw curve as a straight tangent.
physics-stun-quick.transfer: Use the cut layout and identify a rail crossing along the tangent. Test five attempts; watch the initial exit separately from the eventual stopping point.
physics-stun-quick.progression: Change cut angle, then compare how follow/draw move the route away from the reference.

structured-practice-intro-quick.instruction: Choose one saved layout and fixed scoring conditions. Record attempts, pots, position, and legal contact where applicable; note one repeatable error and one adjustment.

practice-aiming-quick.title: Learning to aim accurately

practice-aiming-quick.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
practice-aiming-quick.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
practice-aiming-quick.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
practice-aiming-quick.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

practice-speed-control-quick.purpose: Predict and control stopping distance without changing the aiming line.
practice-speed-control-quick.instruction: Choose a clear path. Name a stopping band, then test low, medium, and higher speeds from the same start. Reset between attempts.
practice-speed-control-quick.success: Record short, inside, or long for five physical attempts at a named band. In the simulator, predict the ordering of three stopping distances.
practice-speed-control-quick.transfer: Use a cue-ball-only route and flat target band. Translate stroke strength by observed travel; simulator speed values are not a measurement of your physical stroke.
practice-speed-control-quick.progression: Narrow the band or add a cushion only after establishing a consistent baseline.

practice-stop-shot-quick.title: Understanding stop shots
practice-stop-shot-quick.purpose: Arrive at a straight full-ball collision without forward or backward roll.
practice-stop-shot-quick.instruction: Use a straight shot with no sidespin. Start slightly below center, keep aim fixed, and adjust one of tip height or speed. Observe the cue-ball center at impact and at rest.

practice-stop-shot-quick.transfer: Use the setup sheet and choose the same stopping tolerance on the cloth. Record pot and stop separately; recreate the original ball centers after every attempt.
practice-stop-shot-quick.progression: Increase approach distance; regain the stop with speed and tip height rather than assuming center-tip contact always means stun.

pool-follow-control-quick-draw-control-q.transfer: Place a flat visual target beyond contact. Reproduce the layout and aim for the same finish; judge your stroke by travel rather than copying a slider percentage.
pool-follow-control-quick-draw-control-q.progression: Use a smaller zone only after consistent pocketing and position; then increase approach distance.

pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.title: Impact cue ball / overlap
pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.purpose: Connect the chosen pocket, object-ball contact, and cue-ball approach.
pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.instruction: Name the pocket. Observe the ghost-ball center and contact line. Execute Shot, reset, then change only aim. Compare a full hit with a small cut.
pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.success: For each of five attempts, record the intended pocket and whether the object ball entered it. Separate an aim miss from a positional miss.
pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.transfer: Place the ball centers using the setup sheet. Visualize the ghost-ball center while standing, align the cue, and deliver the shot. Use five physical attempts; the software cannot measure your alignment or stroke.
pool-ghost-ball-quick-ball-overlap-quick.progression: Increase cue-ball distance or cut angle, one at a time, after a repeatable baseline.

main-pick-and-play-full-racks.title: Pick and Play Full Racks
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.purpose: Use Pick and Play Full Racks correctly within the current lesson.
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.instruction: Pick and Play Full Racks prepares a complete game rack. Choose 3-Ball, 6-Ball, 7-Ball, 8-Ball, 9-Ball, 10-Ball, Ultimate 8 Ball, or Straight Pool from the menu, then press Start. Six Ball uses a small triangle. Seven Ball places the seven in the center of a hexagon. Straight Pool prepares fourteen balls with the front position open. Add a single ball if you want a separate break ball, then drag it and the cue ball to your preferred positions. Ultimate 8 Ball uses the fixed numbered arrangement and puts the eight ball exactly on the foot spot.
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.success: Record the game, starting layout, legal balls cleared, scratches, and first lost position. Compare two attempts from the same post-break layout, not different random breaks.
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.transfer: Use a correctly racked game or reproduce a saved post-break layout. Observe the chosen game rules yourself; the lesson does not automatically referee the run.
main-pick-and-play-full-racks.progression: Improve the earliest weak transition before increasing layout difficulty.

practice-speed-contact-baseline.title: Speed and contact baseline
practice-speed-contact-baseline.purpose: Arrive at a straight full-ball collision without forward or backward roll.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.instruction: Use a straight shot with no sidespin. Start slightly below center, keep aim fixed, and adjust one of tip height or speed. Observe the cue-ball center at impact and at rest.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.success: Count five attempts: record the pot and a cue-ball finish within one ball diameter of its center at impact. Count a pot with unwanted roll as a position miss.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.transfer: Use the setup sheet and choose the same stopping tolerance on the cloth. Record pot and stop separately; recreate the original ball centers after every attempt.
practice-speed-contact-baseline.progression: Increase approach distance; regain the stop with speed and tip height rather than assuming center-tip contact always means stun.

practice-target-landing.title: Target landing precision
practice-target-landing.purpose: Pocket the current ball while preserving a usable angle on the next ball.
practice-target-landing.instruction: Name the next ball and pocket first. Mark a cue-ball zone and explain the angle it preserves. Execute Shot, inspect the actual simulated leave, and compare one speed or tip adjustment.
practice-target-landing.success: Use the existing target size chosen for this plan. Count only a pot plus cue-ball center inside the target. The narrated goal is 8 of 10; begin with a larger zone if needed.
practice-target-landing.transfer: Set both object balls from the diagram. Play the first shot, then play the second from where the cue ball actually stops; no repositioning between those two shots.
practice-target-landing.progression: Shrink the useful zone or add a third ball; do not count an attractive leave that is blocked.

practice-rock-around-clock.title: Rock Around the Clock

practice-rock-around-clock.instruction: Compare two orders on the same layout. Explain the next-ball angle before each shot. Use Shot 2, execute one shot at a time, and revise from the resulting layout.

practice-rock-around-clock.transfer: Choose 8-ball-style open practice or lowest-ball-first rotation before starting. Play each run from the actual leaves; reset only at the end of a run.
practice-rock-around-clock.progression: Add a ball or a blocker while retaining a readable, explained pattern.

practice-one-rail-kick.title: One-rail kick reference
practice-one-rail-kick.purpose: Reach the legal target through a cushion route when direct access is blocked.
practice-one-rail-kick.instruction: Name the target and required rail sequence. Keep speed and sidespin consistent while adjusting only the first rail aim point. Check that the blocker is avoided.
practice-one-rail-kick.success: Record target first-contact, scratch, and the game-required rail/pot condition on five attempts. A target touch is a contact score, not automatically a legal shot.
practice-one-rail-kick.transfer: Copy the blocker and target. Identify the cushion-nose contact by diamond reference; reset all balls after each escape.
practice-one-rail-kick.progression: Aim for four target contacts in five as a suggested practice goal, then change the starting diamond.
